title: Government's EV targets expected to be reduced this week
summary:
The UK government's electric vehicle (EV) targets are expected to be reduced this week in a move likely to be welcomed by carmakers but opposed by environmental groups.
But the speed of the transition to electric has been hotly debated, including within the cabinet.
Asked about reports the targets would be reduced, Burnham dismissed this as "speculation", adding: "No decision has been made at this point."
The Society of Motor Manufacturers and Traders welcomed the government's review of the EV targets when it was announced in the summer.
He said the government's targets could not be achieved "without putting at risk any future investment".

title: Turkiye pushes electrification top of climate agenda as COP31 set to open
summary:
Ankara aims to make electricity account for 35 percent of global energy demand by 2035.
Share Turkiye pushes electrification top of climate agenda as COP31 set to open on social mediaThe United Nations climate conference COP31 is set to open on Monday in Antalya, Turkiye, against the backdrop of the US-led war on Iran, which has underscored the world’s attachment to fossil fuels.
Turkiye has said it would centre electrification on the COP31 agenda, launching the non-binding 35-by-35 Global Electrification Pledge, which aims to make electricity account for at least 35 percent of global energy demand by 2035.
Turkiye says the “35 by 35” will speed up the shift to renewable sources of energy while strengthening energy security.
This has set up a debate on whether electrification alone should count as climate progress.

title: Smog blankets New Delhi as Diwali firecrackers worsen air quality
summary:
Air quality in Indian capital reaches severe levels, posing heightened health risks for more than 30 million residents.
Share Smog blankets New Delhi as Diwali firecrackers worsen air quality on social mediaHeavy smog has blanketed New Delhi after firecrackers lit up the Indian capital during Diwali celebrations, worsening the seasonal pollution crisis.
Last month, India’s Supreme Court put in place restrictions to limit Diwali pollution, allowing only approved “green firecrackers” under specified conditions for three-hour windows on Saturday and Sunday.
Seasonal pollutionOn Wednesday, days before Diwali, toxic air pollution in New Delhi surged to more than 30 times the WHO’s recommended daily limit, data from air monitors showed.
AdvertisementVehicles account for 23 percent of New Delhi’s winter pollution, while biomass burning, including farm stubble fires, contributes 20 percent, according to India’s Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change.

title: North Pennines National Landscape prepares for climate change
summary:
Climate change readiness and helping people access the countryside are among priorities in a five-year plan for a national landscape.
The North Pennines National Landscape Management Plan 2026-31 has been adopted by the Cumberland, Westmorland and Furness, County Durham and Northumberland councils.
Chris Woodley-Stewart, director of the North Pennines National Landscape (NPNL), said: "In many ways, its the most ambitious plan that we've ever had, but also the most realistic."
National landscapes were formerly known as areas of outstanding natural beauty, and the North Pennines features heather moors, dales, woods and one of England's highest waterfalls High Force.
One of the priorities in its management plan announced last month was adapting to "warmer, wetter winters and hotter, drier summers".

title: El Niño pushes world towards record heat as COP31 opens
summary:
The world is on course for its hottest year on record as the planet is hit with warming from climate change and El Niño, scientists have told BBC News.
The warning comes as world leaders and negotiators gather in Turkey on Monday for the opening of COP31, the latest UN climate summit.
"We have had a run of record warm years," said Dr Robert Rohde, of Berkeley Earth.
On Friday, the EU's Copernicus climate service, external confirmed that October was the hottest on record.
It said that 2027 will provide no let-up, as an unusually powerful El Niño will continue into next year, pushing temperatures higher.

title: Climate talks will be tougher at COP31 amid heightened global tensions: Grace Fu
summary:
SINGAPORE: Talks at COP31 this year are expected to be tougher than in previous years amid heightened global tensions and competing domestic priorities, said Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu.
"The attention on climate has to be called for, and it's important for COP31 that we draw the global attention of political leaders on global climate action,” she added.
SINGAPORE AT COPAs the world gathers for COP31, Singapore will be organising a country pavilion to showcase its commitment to climate action, innovation and partnerships.
She said that Singapore can “bring energy" to global climate talks.
Ms Fu said she hoped the pavilion could serve as a platform for announcing and initiating projects that translate climate commitments into action.
